summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of diabetes, kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and prior toe amputations was admitted for IV antibiotic treatment of resistant E. coli and Prevotella osteomyelitis in the right foot following a recent amputation. He was started on imipenem in the hospital and transitioned to outpatient ertapenem for a four-week course. A PICC line was successfully placed via the right brachial vein under ultrasound and fluoroscopic guidance to facilitate antibiotic delivery. During the admission, his blood pressure was elevated, prompting an increase in chlorthalidone dose. He remained afebrile with stable labs and no signs of systemic infection. Blood cultures were negative. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue wound care, immunosuppressants, and insulin, and to follow up with primary and infectious disease clinics.
